**Date:** {{< meta display-date >}}  
**From:** {{< meta from-address >}}  
**Manuscript Location:** {{< meta manuscript-location >}}  

My dear Cousin Mary[^1],
I am glad you like my books. I think there are one or two more that you have not seen, [the Stokesley Secret](../books.html#40) which is about the size of [Countess Kate](../books.html#44), and is most of it fun, [Kenneth](../books.html#10), which is about a boy and girl in the Retreat from Moscow, and some short stories for poor children, called [Langley School](../books.html#9), [Friarswood Post office](../books.html#36), [Leonard the Lion heart](../books.html#26) and [Ben Sylvester’s Word](../books.html#25)
your affectionate cousin

C M Yonge

[^1]: The letter is obviously addressed to a child, and is catalogued in the Coleridge collection at Texas. [Mary Elizabeth Coleridge](../persons.html#350) (1861-1907) is suggested as a possibility.

None of the books mentioned was published later than 1862.
